steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The rock cycle is a continuous process where rocks are transformed between igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic types

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Igneous rocks form from cooling magma/lava; weathering and erosion break them into sediment then sedimentary rocks

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sedimentary rocks can be metamorphosed by heat/pressure to metamorphic rocks; or melted to magma then igneous rocks

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Metamorphic rocks can be weathered/eroded to sedimentary rocks; or melted to magma then igneous rocks

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Describe a complete path through the rock cycle starting from an igneous rock. | Q: What are the two main energy sources driving the rock cycle? | Q: Can a metamorphic rock become a sedimentary rock directly?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Granite (igneous) to weathering/erosion to sediment transport to deposition to compaction and cementation to sandstone (sedimentary) to heat and pressure to quartzite (metamorphic) to further heating/ | Internal heat from Earth's core (drives melting, metamorphism, plate tectonics, volcanism) and external solar energy (drives weathering, erosion, transport, and deposition by water, wind and ice). | Yes, metamorphic rocks exposed at the surface can be weathered and eroded into sediment, which is then transported, deposited and lithified into sedimentary rock.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know ALL possible paths between the three rock types, not just one circular route External processes (Sun-driven): weathering, erosion, transport, deposition Internal processes (core heat-driven): melting, metamorphism, tectonism, uplift Be able to trace a specific path (e.g. from sedimentary to igneous)
